placements.why: src-1 states a settled behavioral rule of the system (saving a memory enrolls its creator as a reviewer) — a mechanism-level specification. No strata exist yet in this repo, and nothing in Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Organization/Proof/Templates/Calibration (as named in the taxonomy) is a closer fit than a category for system mechanism/behavior; minting Architecture as the first real strata category this content calls for.
placements.title: System behavior and mechanism specification as its own organizational tier
placements.frame: Does this describe how a system component is built or behaves, as opposed to why it exists (Opportunity/Strategy) or how it's marketed (Product)?

placements.title: Memory creation automatically establishes the creator's review authority
placements.frame: Does the act of creating/saving a memory alone justify granting its creator standing as a reviewer, or should that enrollment depend on something further?
placements.why: src-1 asserts, as a settled 'Decision,' that the e2e suite treats saving a memory as sufficient to enroll its creator as a reviewer — a recurring behavioral rule about how authorship and review authority are linked, the kind of subject future envelopes about review workflows, enrollment triggers, or reviewer-assignment logic would keep feeding. No existing leaf or strata covers this (graph and strata are both empty), so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Architecture strata rather than left as a bare fact.
